The '''European Social Survey''' ('''ESS''') is a social scientific endeavour to map the attitudes, beliefs and behaviour patterns of the various populations in Europe. The average duration of an ESS interview is 60 minutes in British English and data is deposited in the [[ESS Data Portal]] https://ess.sikt.no/en/.<ref>{{cite web|title=ESS Data Portal|url=https://ess.sikt.no/en/|website=sikt.no|access-date=18 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Fitzgerald |first=Rory |title=Advances in Questionnaire Design, Development, Evaluation and Testing |last2=Zavala-Rojas |first2=Diana |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=2020 |isbn=978-1-119-26362-3 |pages=496 |chapter=A Model for Cross-National Questionnaire Design and Pretesting}}</ref>

Professor Rory Fitzgerald is the Director of the ESS which in 2013 became a [[European Research Infrastructure Consortium]] (ERIC). The headquarters are at [[City, University of London]].

When it comes to social surveys, the ESS is viewed as a standard, thanks to the high quality of the data it collects. It is highly valued by academics. <ref name="ESSImpact2022">{{cite web
 |last=Technopolis Group
 |year=2022
 |title=SUSTAIN‑2: Impact study of the European Social Survey (Report commissioned by ESS ERIC)
 |url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/sites/default/files/2023-06/ESS-Impact-Study-2.pdf
 |website=European Social Survey
 |publisher=Technopolis Group
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref>

==History==
The ESS was initiated by the [[European Science Foundation]] under the leadership of [[Roger Jowell|Sir Roger Jowell]] and Max Kaase 1995 and established in 2001 at the [[National Centre for Social Research]] (now NatCen Social Research) in London.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=History |url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/about/history |access-date=September 15, 2023 |website=European Social Surveys}}</ref>

One of the reasons to start this new time series of social scientific data was that existing cross-national attitude surveys were regarded as not of sufficient methodological rigour to draw on as reliable sources for knowledge about changes over time in Europe. Since 2002-2003, a total of 40 countries have participated in at least one round of data collection. In the most recent 2020-2022 ESS Round 10, 32 countries are participating.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Participating Countries |url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/about/participating-countries |access-date=September 15, 2023 |website=European Social Surveys}}</ref>

In 2013, the ESS became an independent legal entity known as an ERIC<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESS ERIC - European Social Survey European Research Infrastructure {{!}} Knowledge for policy |url=https://knowledge4policy.ec.europa.eu/organisation/ess-eric-european-social-survey-european-research-infrastructure_en |access-date=2024-04-09 |website=[[European Commission]]}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> and as of 2020 has 25 Member countries and one Observer country. In 2016, the ESS became a landmark of the ESFRI roadmap in recognition of its consolidation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESS ERIC {{!}} ESFRI Roadmap 2021 |url=https://roadmap2021.esfri.eu/projects-and-landmarks/browse-the-catalogue/ess-eric/ |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=European Strategy Forum on Research Infrastructures (ESFRI)}}</ref>

As of October 2024, there are over 230,000 registered users of the ESS from countries across the world and almost 7,000 publications used the ESS data.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fitzgerald |first=Rory |last2=Aizpurua |first2=Eva |date=2024-12-18 |title=20 Years of the European Social Survey: An Interview with Rory Fitzgerald |url=https://www.surveypractice.org/article/126414-20-years-of-the-european-social-survey-an-interview-with-rory-fitzgerald |journal=Survey Practice |language=en |volume=17 |doi=10.29115/SP-2024-0025 |doi-access=free}}</ref> 

==Scope==
===Themes===
The ESS is composed of a core section, with themes that appear in every round, and a rotating section dedicated to specific themes in specific rounds.
The core section includes the following themes:
*Media use and trust
*Politics
*Well-being, exclusion, religion, discrimination, identity
*Personal and household characteristics
*Socio-demographics
*Human values

The following table includes the themes of the rotating section, including which rounds they appear in. <ref name="ESSDataPortal">{{cite web

==Methodology==
===Sampling===
The ESS is flexible in terms of the choice of sample design, as each country has different sampling resources. However, some requirements should absolutely be respected, and these are mentioned in the Survey Specification of the ESS. 

Firstly, the sampling method should cover the ESS target population as best as possible. This includes all people over the age of 15 who live in a private household. Their nationality or language does not matter.<ref name="ESSRound11Sampling">{{cite web
 |title=European Social Survey Round 11 Sampling Guidelines: Principles and Implementation
 |author=ESS Sampling and Weighting Expert Panel
 |date=2022-07-04
|url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/docs/round11/methods/ESS_Round11_Sampling_Guidelines.pdf
 |website=European Social Survey
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref>

Secondly, [[probability sampling]] should be used at every stage to select individuals. Neither [[quota sampling]] nor substitution of non-responding or non-accessible units is permitted.<ref name="ESSRound11Sampling" />

Thirdly, the design chosen should provide a prescribed level of statistical precision. Therefore, the minimum affective sample size should be of 800 for countries with a population inferior to 2 million inhabitants who are over 15, and of at least 1,500 for other countries. <ref name="Lynn2007">{{cite journal
 |last1=Lynn
 |first1=P.
 |last2=Häder
 |first2=S.
 |last3=Gabler
 |first3=S.
 |last4=Laaksonen
 |first4=S.
 |year=2007
 |title=Methods for achieving equivalence of samples in cross-national surveys: the European Social Survey experience
 |journal=Journal of Official Statistics
 |volume=23
 |issue=1
 |pages=107–124
 |doi=10.2478/v10010-007-0010-2
}}</ref>

===Data collection===
In May 2022, the ESS General Assembly switched to a self-completion design after a recommendation by the Core Scientific Team (CST), rather than conducting face-to-face interviews. This transition is due to a decreased capacity of face-to-face interviewers as well as diminished quality, all while conserving the accuracy of the data. <ref name="ESSDataCollectionF2F">{{cite web
 |title=Data Collection: Face-to-Face – Methodology
|url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/methodology/methodology/data-collection-f2f
 |website=European Social Survey
 |publisher=ESS ERIC
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref><ref name="Lugtig2024ModeDiff">{{cite web
 |last=Lugtig
 |first=P.
 |year=2024
 |title=Comparison of ESS rounds 9 and 10: mode differences
 |url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/sites/default/files/2024-10/round-9-10-comparison-final.pdf
 |website=European Social Survey
 |publisher=ESS ERIC
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref>

Before the data collection, the CST provides a quality report to every country on issues that should be taken into account in the next round. CST members and Field directors meet to discuss standards of data collection. Four weeks before fieldwork starts, the fieldwork questionnaire should be filled in by National Coordinators (NCs), and agreed by the CST. Two weeks before the start of fieldwork, fieldwork projections based on previous rounds should be provided by each countries.<ref name="ESSDataCollectionF2F" />

During data collection, every country should submit weekly fieldwork progress in the form of a dataset to the CST, which is compared to the previously submitted fieldwork projections. This is useful in identifying plausible issues, which survey organizations might need to investigate.<ref name="Koch2009">{{cite journal
 |last1=Koch
 |first1=A.
 |last2=Blom
 |first2=A.
 |last3=Stoop
 |first3=I.
 |last4=Kappelhof
 |first4=J.
 |year=2009
 |title=Data Collection Quality Assurance in Cross-National Surveys: The Example of the ESS
 |journal=Methoden – Daten – Analysen
 |volume=3
 |issue=2
 |pages=219–247
}}</ref>

After data collection, the countries should deposit all fieldwork documents as well as the ESS data set at the ESS Data Archive. They should also provide [[metadata]] in the form of the National Technical Summary, and [[paradata]] in the form of contact form data. The CST then analyzes all quality aspects, including [[interviewer effect|interviewer effects]], sample composition, refusal conversion, and so on.<ref name="ESSDataCollectionF2F" />

===Data processing and archiving===
From the stage when files are deposited to the ESS Archive Intranet until the final approval of the files, 16 data programmes are applied. Each programme is a specific step of the data processing stage, and there are two main ones we can identify. Those two stages are both followed by data processing reports to the NCs.<ref name="ESSDataProcessing">{{cite web
 |title=Data Processing and Archiving – Methodology
 |url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/methodology/ess-methodology/data-processing-and-archiving
 |website=European Social Survey
 |publisher=ESS ERIC
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref>

The first stage is data ingest and data checks, which uses programme 1 to 5. This stage is aimed at improving data quality and standardization as much as possible. Data ingest is about checking formal attributes of the data files, and data checks looks for wild codes and inconsistencies in the data.<ref name="Kolsrud2010">{{cite journal
 |last1=Kolsrud
 |first1=K.
 |last2=Midtsæter
 |first2=H.
 |last3=Orten
 |first3=H.
 |last4=Skjåk
 |first4=K.K.
 |last5=Øvrebø
 |first5=O.P.
 |year=2010
 |title=Processing, Archiving and Dissemination of ESS data: The Work of the Norwegian Social Science Data Services
 |journal=ASK. Research and Methods
 |volume=19
 |issue=1
 |pages=51–92
}}</ref>

The second stage is about editing data, edit controls and approving the final data. It uses programmes 6 to 11. This is about fixing the issues identified in the first stage, meaning recoding the wild codes and assigning missing values when necessary. Once the draft file is approved by the NCs, it can be integrated in the cross-national files.<ref name="Kolsrud2010" />

The [[Norwegian Social Science Data Services]] (NSD) is the official data archive for the ESS since 2002. All data is archived in a safe manner, with three different strategies of preservation:<ref name="Kolsrud2010" />
*Non-digital backups
*[[Emulator|Emulation]], where the original computing environment is recreated on modern systems.
*[[Data migration|Migration]], where digital objects are converted into newer and accessible formats.

==Prizes==
In 2005 the ESS was the winner of the [[Descartes Prize]], an annual European science award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006 |title=Six years of Descartes Prize winners: Excellence in scientific collaborative research and science communication |url=https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/1d62490e-6311-4a62-a41e-d7db3da2a5a5/language-en/format-PDF/source-search |access-date=April 9, 2024 |website=Publications Office of the European Union}}</ref>

In 2020, the ESS was awarded the 2020 [[Lijphart]]/[[Adam Przeworski|Przeworski]]/[[Sidney Verba|Verba]] (LPV) Dataset Award 2020 by the Comparative Politics Section of the [[American Political Science Association]] (APSA).<ref name="CESSDAAward">{{cite web
 |title=ESS receives dataset award
 |url=https://www.cessda.eu/News-Events/News/CESSDA/ESS-receives-dataset-award
 |website=CESSDA
 |publisher=Consortium of European Social Science Data Archives
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref><ref name="ESSAbout">{{cite web
 |title=About the European Social Survey
 |url=https://www.europeansocialsurvey.org/about-ess
 |website=European Social Survey
 |publisher=ESS ERIC
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref>

In 2024, the [[Martin Kohli|Kohli]] Foundation Infrastructure Prize for Sociology was awarded to the ESS.<ref name="KohliPrize2024">{{cite web
 |title=Infrastructure Prize for Sociology 2024: European Social Survey
 |url=https://kohlifoundation.eu/news/infrastructure-prize-for-sociology-2024-european-social-survey/
 |website=Kohli Foundation for Sociology
 |publisher=Kohli Foundation for Sociology
 |date=2024-04-25
 |access-date=2026-01-03
}}</ref><ref name="ESSAbout" />
